main_text.p: artis fallaciam nodum percipientes,qui,si ingenio pollent, coualescere possunt: quibus ut stolidis,aut crassa minerua natis uere conuenit elleborus,uel si peruicax sit affectus,scutica, quàm fatuis ,stultis ac insanis plurimum prodesse satis superq; testantur,diuo Mathurino uoti,qui continuis nouem matutinis,loco potionis uel humorem melancholicum alterantis, uel euacuantis , uerberibus ad cruorem usq; caeduntur:atq; tenui uictu, nempe aqua & pauco pane continentur. Hoc enim pacto fit humoris crassi & lenti non solùm incisio, & attenuatio,sed & eiusdem in contrarium reuulsio. Quare non aspernandum est remedium, quod quidem ἐυπόρισον[?] est, & paratu facile. Quoniam autem impostura non corporis uitium est, sed animae, quòd proximo negotium facesfsit,idcirco medicinae non committitur,sed censurę magistratus,cuius interest in hominum flagitia animaduertere.

page.notes: The Greek word after "quidem" (printed as ἐυπόρισον, probably εὔπορον or a similar form) is uncertain; marked [?]. "poIlent" is read as "pollent". Imprint line "CIↃ. IↃ. LXXIX." is the printed date 1579 in reversed-C numerals, rendered as Roman numerals in capitals per the rule. The lower margin is blank apart from a faint stain.
